name: IBM POWER Memory Model
description: The POWER architecture model allows extensive reorderings and non-multi-copy-atomic (non-MCA) behaviour: a store can be visible to one thread before others. Requires explicit barriers (sync, lwsync, isync) or dependencies for ordering.

mca.note: POWER is the canonical non-multicopy-atomic architecture; Sarkar et al.'s operational storage-subsystem model lets a write propagate to different threads at different times.

catSupport.note: herd7's ppc.cat — the cat model of Alglave, Maranget & Tautschnig, validated against POWER hardware.

katSupport.note: kater ships kat/power-fm.kat and the simplified kat/power-fm-simpl.kat, kat/power-weak.kat and kat/power-fm-orig.kat. Three of them are unusable as comparison targets: power-weak, power-fm-simpl and power-fm-simpl-full carry the term eco*;po?;eco* in ar, and eco* contains the identity, so ar contains po and every containment into ar+ holds vacuously (checked: po <= power-weak::ar+ holds, where po <= tso::tso+ and po <= arm8::ob+ are both refuted). Only power-fm and power-fm-orig are non-degenerate, and against those the IMM compilation query is refuted on a fence-vocabulary gap. The paper notes the full model needs manual rotations to check within reasonable time (§3.7). See litmus/kater/open/compilation-IMM-vs-POWER.kat.
